name: Standing Cable Incline Press
description: A standing chest press performed with cables set at a low position, pressing upward and forward at an incline angle. This replicates the vector of an incline bench press in a standing, free-movement context. The standing position adds core anti-extension demand while the cable maintains constant tension through the full pressing range, particularly at the top where free weights become lighter.

execution.starting_position: Face away from a cable machine with low pulleys set near the floor. Hold both handles with arms bent, hands at lower chest/hip level. Stand in a split stance for stability.
execution.setup_instructions: Set both low pulleys at the lowest position. Attach single D-handles. Stand far enough from the stack to have taut cables at the bottom of the press.
steps: Step 1: Face away from the machine, cables running from low behind you. Hands at hip/lower chest level, elbows bent.
Step 2: Press the handles forward and upward at an incline angle — toward where a high wall meets the ceiling.
Step 3: Fully extend the arms in the incline press direction.
Step 4: Return under control, following the same angled path back to the starting position.
execution.breathing_instructions: Exhale on the press upward, inhale on the controlled return.
common_mistakes: Pressing straight forward instead of upward at the incline angle
Leaning excessively forward, reducing core engagement
Using too much weight, causing the torso to pitch backward
safety_considerations: Keep the core braced to prevent lower back hyperextension
Use a split stance with the same side forward as the dominant pressing arm for stability
execution.range_of_motion_guidance: Full elbow extension at the top. At the bottom, hands are at lower chest level with elbows bent approximately 90 degrees.
coaching_cues: Press up and out — think incline angle, not flat
Keep the chest tall and proud — do not let the torso collapse forward
